Market stance

A capitulation day splits the group into waiters, not buyers: QQQ fell 6.49%, its 4th-largest single-day drop in a decade, SPX broke its three-month range floor, and the only names on the board that still sit above every average are AAPL, MSFT and AMZN — Sean is preparing overextension-reversal buys but says no signal has fired, Remz wants a VIX blow-off into the 30s before going long, and Venu's only call is to DCA index ETFs for long-term investors.

  • Venu's VIX history — after +50% VIX days since 1990, the S&P's median return was +7.5% (3m), +7.7% (6m), +13.2% (12m); watch the VIX back under 20 and wait for a follow-through day
  • DiCarlo's levels — PLTR needs $165 in the next week or $130 is on the table; ONDS revisit at $3.50; ALAB low $200s achieved

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
A capitulation window: Thursday's close was red across the board — SPY −4.41%, QQQ −6.49%, IWM −4.59%, TLT +0.21% — and the group's posts describe a market coming apart at the AI trade, not a dip to buy. Prof supplies the scale: the market lost $3 trillion in a day, “the hammer on AI's head” on the first day after the Democrats' win, and overnight KOSPI fell 8.5% and halted at the open. His QQQ table puts −6.49% as the 4th-largest single-day QQQ decline in the last 10 years, behind only the three March 2020 COVID prints. Remz supplies the structure: SPX down 3%, three months stuck between 7560 and 7840 with lower highs since Oct 1, and today the floor finally gave — the 200-day at 7323 is the test, every dip to it since April 2025 has been bought, and back over 7600 this was a false break. He adds his own trigger: he wants the VIX to push into the 30s, with a blow-off top somewhere in that range, before he starts considering going long. Sean supplies the preparation: the setup he is getting ready for is an OVEREXTENSION REVERSAL, after several hard down days a stock can become unusually extended — but getting close to a setup is NOT the same as getting a buy signal, and his list is MRVL, SMH, LITE, STX, DDOG, COHR, EISC and PENG. He also flags the prior all-time-high breakout spots: QQQ at 635.87 and SMH at 426.05, where the strongest names try to build out and hold. iain supplies the discipline: the last three weeks have been a reminder that knowing when to hit the brakes matters as much as knowing when to floor it, judged by his equity curve, market conditions, leadership and setup quality — and he notes account blowups posted today, “markets like this have a funny way of exposing who actually understands risk mang.” Enrich supplies the patience: capitulation today, bulls didn't step in, VIX elevated and IV on some growth names 200%+ with no earnings ahead, so premiums need to cool before getting aggressive — being right on direction won't mean much if IV crush eats the move. He is focused on real revenue, manageable debt and valuations getting more attractive, his daily DCAs are turned up, bigger chunk buys come when a bottom builds and holds, and he is not catching a falling knife. He adds that after-hours buyers need to show up tomorrow, that he thinks “we're close to a bottom, but it won't be a straight line back up,” and to watch PDL — Yahoo returns no trading data for PDL, so it gets no row. Venu supplies the history and the only long call: the VIX up over 60% in a day, and across the 10 such instances since 1990 the S&P 500's median return was +7.5% in 3 months, +7.7% in 6 months and +13.2% in 12 months, up 7–8 of 10 — with the failures being 1990 (recession) and 2021 (Fed hikes, bear market) — plus his rule to watch the VIX fall back under 20 and wait for a follow-through day. For long-term or new investors he would consider starting to DCA into VOO and VGT; for swing and position traders, staying in cash is the frame (his post is truncated at that line). He also repeats O'Neil's lesson: in corrections, watch the stocks that corrected least from their all-time highs — the strongest hold up better. DiCarlo supplies the levels: PLTR needs back over $165 in the next week or $130 is on the table, ONDS is a revisit at $3.50 with the cycle over, and ALAB's low $200s have been achieved. Your process gives no clean qualifier today — nothing is a constructive pullback, a tightening base near highs, or a confirmed breakout; the closest to strength are AAPL, MSFT and AMZN, still above every average, and the rest of the board is tests to survive: NVDA on its 3-month low, GOOGL's $270 test still live, SMH 4.84% above Sean's 426.05 line, and KLAC's short with targets 125 and 100. The discipline is in the framing: watch the reversal list and the ATH spots, wait for Remz's VIX 30s or Venu's follow-through day, and do not chase a falling knife.
